newsitem.title: UK: Sears in talks with Littlewoods over Freemans.
newsitem.headline: Sears in talks with Littlewoods over Freemans.

text.p: Sears Plc said it was in advanced discussion with Littlewoods for the disposal of its mail order business Freemans.

Sears said in a statement that the sale would be conditional on the agreement of terms and the approval of shareholders, and would be subject to the Office of Fair Trading indicating that it would not refer the acquisition of Freemans to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
Sears gave no details of the expected size of the bid but the Financial Times newspaper said Littlewoods was prepared to pay about 350 million sterling for Freemans.
Freemans is Britain's third largest mail order business and several companies, including two from France and Germany, are thought to have been interested in buying.
Analysts at Merrill Lynch this week rated the Sears stock "reduce" and lowered earnings estimates, market sources said.

They said that for the current year ended January 1997 Merrill cut its estimate for Sears' pre-tax profit to 100 million stg from 115 million, reflecting a poor performance in the company's shoe retail operations and mail order division.
In September Sears posted a 3.7 percent rise in pre-tax, pre-exceptional profits to 28 million stg.
